rule: Use the body for what the body can express. Use the icon for what must remain after the body is gone.

candidates.reason: Pointing can identify a participant live; a durable safety or travel artifact may still require a neutral person.
candidates.suggested_role: neutral participant for travel, safety and interpersonal composition

candidates.reason: A visible building can be indicated live; an unattended destination or shelter message needs the generic concept to remain.
candidates.suggested_role: generic shelter/destination distinct from named venue types

candidates.reason: Gaze and pointing work live; an accessibility or attention cue must encode the concept when unattended.
candidates.suggested_role: look/see cue for accessibility and signage

candidates.reason: Visible clothing can be pointed to; remote packing or identification instructions may need an explicit object concept.
A person can indicate a body location live; a stored medical message must preserve where the issue is.
Heat is not reliably visible or gestureable, and warnings must remain understandable without a communicator.
Cold is not reliably visible or gestureable, and comfort or safety instructions can outlast the exchange.
Relative scale can be demonstrated live; remote selection instructions may need size encoded.
A visible color can be pointed to live; remote object identification needs the color to survive in the artifact.
Voice, phone, or a note can supply the channel live; a channel-neutral interface cue may need an explicit message concept.
Ambient light can be indicated live; an unattended visibility, lighting, or access instruction may need it encoded.
candidates.suggested_role: lighting, visibility, or access cue distinct from a celestial-body reading

candidates.reason: The physical container is usually pointable; standalone demand remains unproven, so keep the proposal deferred.
A visible animal can be indicated directly; standalone warning demand remains too broad and unproven.
Speaker roles, pointing, and a neutral person can supply participants; grammatical person and gender are outside current scope.
These operators would copy language-specific syntax rather than solve an independently demonstrated Pictiq task.
candidates.suggested_role: copy Toki Pona syntax into tiles
